entries.text: Hi there — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 25 minutes to do this — it really means a lot. Honestly, the more you can share with me, the better — we're aiming for about fifteen hundred words of feedback together, so please don't worry about going long. The founders read every word of these chats, so what you say actually shapes what HD does next. As a thank-you you'll get a $75 discount code at the end. So — to kick us off, tell me about your mining setup right now. What are you running, where, and what are you trying to figure out next?

Yeah. Right now, I am running a few machines. I am running a NerdQX plus plus I am also running the Nerd OctX three point one release. Uh, Bitaxe, and then I'm running a solo node on a future bit. And on its way to me is the future bit uh, solo node, an eighteen terahash unit. I'm also looking to get improved power supply. And, uh, I like what healing deploy has been doing lately. So I'm looking to see if I can get a nerd q x or maybe something that's in the neighborhood of ten to fifteen terahash All of this in the next week or so.
Whoa — that's
That's it.

Whoa — that's a serious fleet. NerdQAxe++, NerdOctaxe 3.1, Bitaxe, Future Bit solo node, plus an 18 TH unit incoming — you're deep in this.

Let me pull up the NerdQAxe you've been eyeing — I noticed you've come back to it quite a few times over the last couple weeks. So you already own a NerdQAxe++ — and you're looking at this one again. What's pulling you back?

The price is about fifty percent less than what I paid a few months ago uh, with the improved chipset. It looks like I'm able to get it just above six terahash. Which right now on my QAX, I'm not able to get above six. Unless I get a four hundred watt power supply.

Got it — so the unit you already own is cap····6 unless you upgrade the PSU, and this new rev hits 6+ out of the box at half the price you paid. That's a real reason to come back.

You mentioned the 400W power supply — tell me about that. Are you already shopping for one, and where are you looking?

I am looking I've looked at Jingle Miner and, uh, bit x dot as well. Uh, but right now, I haven't looked see if he'll Helium Deploy has those units. But I need a I power supply that isn't encased in plastic. And is able to handle quite a bit more pull from the QX that I can get those improved cache rates with not, oh, without not overheating or frankly, blowing a fuse.

Jingle Miner and Bitaxe.dot — okay, noted. Those are competitors we should be tracking.

And the "not encased in plastic" detail — that's interesting. Why does that matter for you specifically? Is it a heat thing, or something else?

I I think it it comes down to a matter of not only the heat, but the fire risk quite frankly. These plastic units tend to retain a lot more heat. There isn't heat dissipation on this power supply. Whereas, these commercial metal with a heat sink fan built in, uh, tend to run a lot more reliably and do not run as hot.

Fire risk — that's a real concern, not just a preference. Especially with a fleet your size running 24/7.

So you're basically piecing together server-grade PSUs because the stock ones feel like a liability. Where are you actually buying the metal/heat-sink PSUs from today — Amazon? eBay? A specific vendor?

Right now, what I'm looking at for one is JingleMiner for my NerdQX which I ordered one, but they sent me the incorrect one. I needed a barrel plug, and they sent me an eight pin connector. So dealing with that issue right now, and I think that's one of the biggest issues right now. Is seeing how I can buy things that are already in stock in North America versus having to wait on getting things direct from China. Which, you know, number one, the customer support isn't always the best. And you're sometimes left at a loss on is it gonna be here, how long it's gonna take. The last order I had for a single power unit took over two weeks. They sent me the wrong one. So that's one of the reasons why I'm looking at helium Deploy, and I'm also looking at Bitronics to see what they can send me. Pardon me, as well. So, you know, that's the biggest thing is what can I find that's here with direct to consumer? I try at times to stay away from eBay because everything is refurbished. And when it comes to certain types of hardware, you really don't wanna deal with a refurbished.

Ah — so the real job is "in-stock in North America, direct-to-consumer, not refurb." China lead times, wrong parts shipped, two-week waits, no support — that's the pain. And HD and Bitronics are who you're triangulating between right now.

You said you like "what HD has been doing lately." What specifically? What's caught your eye?

I think what I've known is and specifically, frankly, as I see it a lot on my Instagram feed, is the improved chip set. Right? The newer chip set But I think the fact that you all are staying away from what has historically been a plastic encased PSU that is usually two hundred watts. Uh, I think from the initial research that I've done with Helium Deploy is these are four hundred watt units with built in fan cooling, uh, where you can run multiple units which I really don't want to do, uh, for this type of standard. I also like to look. If I'm gonna be running multiple miners, off of one PSU, I look at the gold standard silver. Uh, as well and making sure that I have the right pins uh, pin connections. I like what Helium Deploy has with the avoidance of the barrel plug. I cannot stand those barrel plugs. Uh, they just don't seem reliable to me.

Okay so — newer chipset, 400W metal PSU with built-in fan, the gold/silver efficiency standard, and away from barrel plugs. You're paying attention to the engineering specifics in a way most buyers aren't.

The I. feed thing is interesting — is that HD's own account you're following, or are you seeing HD show up via someone else's content?
No. I am following h t directly on Instagram, and then you all are following you all are coming up on my Instagram advertisements and on my feed almost multiple times a day.

Got it — so both organic follow and paid retargeting hitting you. That's useful for us to know it's landing.

Now — you've got NerdQAxe++, NerdOctaxe 3.1, a Bitaxe, a Future Bit solo node, and an 18TH unit incoming. That's five+ machines. Where do they all physically live in your house?

Um, I have them spread out quite frankly. The heat's one of those issues. Right? Uh, I used to run them in my basement because the basement runs about ten degrees cooler than the rest of the house. So as an example, I have my upstairs in in an upstairs office I have my Autax Alpha. In my office downstairs along with my nerd QX and the, uh, Futurebit solo node. Uh, once I get these two new units, I will more than likely move the QX plus plus uh, upstairs with the BitX, and then run, uh, a couple units from my office downstairs next to the, uh, future bit solo node.

So you're actively load-balancing them across rooms for heat management. That's not casual.

And summer's coming — you in a hot climate? Does the heat change what you run or when you run it?

I don't run-in a hot climate. You know? I'm in the I'm I. at a higher elevation. Know, it does get warm in the summer. You know, high is in the low nineties. Uh, so right now, it's not just about heat to dissipation, but it's also load on the homes, uh, electrical. Right? I gotta make sure that I'm running off of different circuits within my power panel. So that I'm not blowing, uh, fuses at the panel. So, you know, I gotta keep everything balanced. Uh, I've generally, the the main floor of my home stays cool. I have refrigerated air. Uh, as long as I keep my home at seventy degrees, uh, Fahrenheit, things tend to be pretty well a runoff. You know? And that's one of the big things is I can't let these I can't let these units and their power supplies get too warm because it just becomes too much of an issue.

Right — so it's a two-axis problem. Heat dissipation AND circuit load across the panel. You're literally mapping which miner goes on which breaker.

Have you ever tripped one? Or had a close call?

I have tripped rakers in the past, frankly, and, uh, back in the day when I was running, uh, Bitcoin and Litecoin nodes, I had to have my basement rewired with a separate panel and improved, uh, outlets to make sure that I could run something a little bit heftier. Uh, but as it relates to my current situation, uh, as an example, I run a window unit in my upstairs master bedroom, which is on the same circuit as my office. So if I don't move things around in my house, then the circuit will trip. So I have to be very cognizant and, uh, I guess, educated in how my electrical panel is drawing throughout the house to make sure that there's no issues.

Wow — you literally had a separate panel installed back in the Litecoin days. You've been at this a long time.

Let me ask — when you're tuning these units, are you doing any overclocking or firmware tweaking? Or running them at stock?

I am tweaking them I'm running increased wattage and voltage. I also make sure to adjust the fan on manual, uh, you know, ideally for me personally, I want to keep everything under fifty nine degrees Celsius. As far as the temperature of the the the voltage regulators and the overall board. Uh, you know, I I wish, quite frankly, that the PSUs had some sort of temperature monitor. So that I could kind of elevate what I'm trying to do as well.

Oh — that's a real product insight. PSU with built-in temp monitoring. Nobody's doing that and it's an obvious gap if you're someone who actually cares about thermal headroom.

Where do you go to learn this stuff? The voltage tweaking, the 59°C target, fan curves — Discord? Reddit? YouTube?

So, frankly, I do do YouTube, which sometimes is a little bit of annoyance because you got a bunch of people who are basically just taking a bunch of sponsorships and whatnot, which is fine. I'm not against that. So what I've learned over the last, uh, six seven years is through experience, you know, learning how to build and improve boards, for example, off of a a Litecoin, uh, Antminer. Things like that. But I do watch some videos. I do go to Reddit. Uh, don't really approach Discord a whole lot even though I I am on it, but I try to see what I can do through through trial and error. And then just seeing what, uh, I see on YouTube from experience with people who aren't really going overboard too much. I'm trying to horror, uh, things off and and just make money off of, uh, what people are sending them.

Yeah — the sponsorship noise on YouTube is real. So you're mostly running it off seven years of hands-on, with YouTube and Reddit as occasional sanity checks. That's a different cohort than the average buyer.

One thing I'm curious about — when you compare miners before buying, do you use a spreadsheet, a site, or just kind of... in your head?

I do I don't keep anything on his side. I do track things, uh, on my Mac. Right? Uh, I I I sometimes will track it in Excel. Uh, I usually will will take my notepad to see what's working. Track, you know, uh, what wattage uh, what frequency things are going at, and just seeing how I can tweak things. Because, ideally, I wanna get the most amount of hash rate with the lowest amount of, uh, power usage. Uh, so, yeah, it's it's in multi ultimately, I've got a pretty good memory. So a lot of times, I'm I have to go mind dumps into my brain to see, okay, what works and what doesn't work.

Got it — Excel + Notepad + memory, optimizing for hashrate-per-watt. The classic engineer's approach.

Let me show you something — there's a comparison table on the HD homepage I want to see if you've come across. Did you scroll past this when you were on the site? Four miners side-by-side — Bitaxe Gamma, NerdQAxe++, NerdOctaxe, Nexus S1.

I did not scroll past it. I did see it on the main page, and it was something that I found very useful as a matter of fact. Because it not only gives you the price, the hash rate, the power draw, if there's any delays in shipping, so on and so forth.
Awesome — so it actually did work for you. What was missing, though? Anything you wished was a column there that isn't?

I think the type of power unit, you know, a lot of people, uh, try to escape that. Power units and power supplies are something that are very important to mining. So you wanna stay away from the plastic encased devices. Get something that's got its own built in cooling fan. So, uh, you know, y'all are showing the power draw. But I think actually showing the type of power supply unit and the type of connector is something that's pretty key. Uh, alongside the the voltage and the amperage Uh, as as far as I'm concerned, other consumers, I guess, may not find use out of it.

That's gold — PSU type, connector type, voltage, amperage. You're saying the comparison table treats the PSU as an afterthought when it's actually the #1 reliability factor. Noted, that's going straight to the founders.

Quick one — let me show you something we're researching. We're thinking about offering a $35 Ethernet add-on — small RJ45 adapter that snaps onto a miner so you can run wired instead of WiFi. Would something like that matter for your setup?

Oh, hell. Yeah. I I I would much rather run things on the wire versus Wi Fi. Uh, you get more consistent uh, connection. You don't get as much drops. You know, with me, I'm on a mesh network at home. Uh, I'm savvy enough that I have to attach my minors to a specific, uh, mesh unit to make sure that there's no drop. So think it's something that would be welcomed.

Perfect — "hell yeah" is the answer we wanted. And the mesh-network detail is great context — you're literally pinning miners to specific mesh nodes to avoid drops. That's a workaround for a real pain.

Would you actually pay $35 per unit for it, given you've got five+ miners? Or does that math start to bite?
I would consider it. Yes.

Good. Even at $35 × 5+ miners it's worth it to you. That tells us a lot.

Okay, switching gears — you mentioned you order from Jingle Miner, you're looking at Bitronics, you've dealt with direct-from-China. What about Solo Satoshi, Compass Mining, Bitcoin Merch — any of those in your rotation?
I have purchased from Bitcoin merge and Solo Satoshi, uh, and then I've also bought direct from, uh, FutureBit, Apollo.

Cool — so Bitcoin Merch, Solo Satoshi, FutureBit direct, plus the China vendors. You've shopped widely.

Of all of them, who do you actually trust the most when something goes wrong? Like, the wrong-PSU-shipped scenario you mentioned — who handles it best?

You know, I my bit my Bitcoin merch, I was hesitant about ordering from them because they are pricey, but my NerdQ ax basically went dead a few weeks after buying it. Uh, they were pretty responsive. They replaced it with warranty, sent me a new unit. So they've been pretty reliable.

Yeah — Bitcoin Merch overcharges but actually honors warranty fast. That's the trade.

How does HD compare on that dimension in your head? You haven't bought from HD yet — what would make you pull the trigger versus going back to Bitcoin Merch or Jingle Miner?

Frankly, what I've seen the last few weeks from you guys in lowering the prices and the seventy five dollar store credit you're getting ready to send me is going to allow me to pull the trigger on that one. And not only order a new solo miner, but also probably order some, uh, PSUs

Ha — well, the $75 is doing its job then. Honestly that's useful for us to know, because we debate internally whether the credit moves the needle or just feels like a nice gesture. For you it's literally tipping the decision.

One more thing I want to test with you — given you're competitively-minded about hashrate-per-watt and tracking your fleet's performance... We're considering a leaderboard inside the HD customer dashboard — opt-in, ranks everyone by hashrate, you'd see where you stack up. Would you actually use that, or does it feel cringe?

It doesn't feel cringe. I think it's something to be useful to compare myself you know, rather than having to go directly to the, uh, the, uh, Bitcoin, uh, Mempool space site to see how the entire, uh, space is doing. I think it'd be nice to see how I'm doing versus basically other hobbyist miners. Uh, I tend to track everything in my own, uh, future bit, uh, and the GUI on each of the miners pages. So it's there's nothing cringe about it. I think it's a great comparison to see how people are doing in relation to hashrate and, uh, JUULs as well.

Mempool.space — okay, that's the workaround. You go there for the macro view but there's no peer-cohort comparison. The leaderboard fills that gap for you specifically.

And you mentioned Joules — so efficiency, not just raw hashrate. We should probably rank on both columns.

Hey, this has been incredibly rich — you've given us a ton. Before we wrap, is there anything we didn't cover that you wish I'd asked about? Anything on your mind about HD or mining in general?
No. I think this has been a great conversation, and I appreciate all taking my insight. And I ultimately appreciate that store credit as well.

Awesome — thank you so much, genuinely. You've given us things we did not have before: the PSU-as-fire-risk lens, the "in-stock in North America" being the real job, the missing PSU column on the comparison table, the mesh-network ethernet workaround, the temp-monitor PSU product idea. All of that's going straight to the founders.

The $75 code will hit your inbox shortly — happy PSU shopping. Take care!
Thanks, Sarah. You too.
Have a wonderful day!
